speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy with feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To help me understand what is wrong, can you tell me if these symptoms have been getting worse over time, and do you notice any vomiting or changes in your bowel movements?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: The tenderness on abdominal palpation and worsening fussiness suggest an acute surgical abdomen. Has the baby passed any stool or gas recently, and do you notice any bilious (green) vomiting? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound showing normal readings contradicts the X-ray findings, suggesting the obstruction may be partial or atypical. Given the bilious vomiting risk and distension, has the baby passed any green vomit or had any bowel movements in the last 12 hours? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_CT_Scan.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Intestinal Atresia (likely Jejunal or Ileal).

The combination of a complete small bowel obstruction (dilated loops, no rectal gas) with normal ultrasound and CT findings in an 8-month-old strongly suggests a congenital atresia rather than an acquired adhesive or intussusception, which would typically show more specific structural abnormalities on imaging. The feeding difficulties and abdominal distension are consistent with the mechanical blockage preventing passage of contents.
